title: Reflected cross-site scripting (XSS)
description: A request parameter is returned in the response without contextual output encoding, so attacker-supplied script runs in the victim's browser.
impact: An attacker can run script in a victim's session, steal session data or perform actions as the victim.

title: Stored cross-site scripting (XSS)
description: User-supplied content is saved and later rendered to other users without output encoding.
impact: Script runs for every user who views the content, which can lead to account takeover and data theft.

3. TODO: describe the observed response that proves the issue.
remediation: Encode output for the correct context, sanitise rich text with a vetted library, and use a strict Content-Security-Policy.

title: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
description: A state-changing request can be triggered from another site because it carries no unpredictable anti-forgery token and relies only on ambient cookies.
impact: An attacker can make a logged-in victim perform unwanted actions such as changing settings or submitting transactions.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. TODO: state the exact URL / endpoint tested.

2. TODO: describe the request, parameter and test input used.

3. TODO: describe the observed response that proves the issue.
remediation: Add per-session anti-CSRF tokens to state-changing requests, set SameSite cookie attributes and verify Origin/Referer headers.

title: Insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
description: Object identifiers supplied by the user are accepted without checking that the requester is allowed to access that object.
impact: Users can read or change other users' data by altering an identifier.

3. TODO: describe the observed response that proves the issue.

impact: An attacker may reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints that are not exposed to the internet.

title: Clickjacking (missing frame protection)
description: Pages can be embedded in frames on other sites because no frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options policy is set.
impact: Users may be tricked into clicking hidden interface elements.

1. TODO: state the exact URL / endpoint tested.

title: Missing HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is not sent.
impact: Users on hostile networks may be downgraded to unencrypted HTTP.
remediation: Send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains once all subdomains support HTTPS.

title: Missing Content-Security-Policy
description: No Content-Security-Policy header is set, removing a defence-in-depth control against script injection.
impact: The impact of any injection flaw is higher without a restrictive policy.
remediation: Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, starting in report-only mode and tightening over time.

title: Session cookie missing security attributes
description: Session cookies lack the Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite attributes.
impact: Cookies may be sent over insecure connections, read by script or sent in cross-site requests.
remediation: Set Secure, HttpOnly and an appropriate SameSite value on all session cookies.

title: Weak TLS configuration
description: The server supports outdated protocol versions or weak cipher suites.
impact: Traffic may be exposed to downgrade or decryption attacks under some conditions.
remediation: Allow only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with strong cipher suites and keep certificates valid and renewed.

description: The domain's public DNS records show missing or permissive email authentication policies.
impact: Attackers may be able to send spoofed email that appears to come from the organisation.
remediation: Publish SPF and DKIM records and move DMARC to an enforcing policy after monitoring.

title: Staff susceptible to phishing
description: During the authorised exercise, a portion of targeted staff opened the lure and interacted with it.
impact: Phishing is a realistic initial access route into the organisation.
remediation: Run regular awareness training, add easy reporting for suspicious email and strengthen email filtering.

title: Valid accounts obtained by password spraying
description: Common passwords were accepted by a number of accounts on an externally reachable service.
impact: Attackers can gain initial access without exploiting software.
remediation: Enforce multi-factor authentication, block common passwords and alert on spray patterns.

title: Lateral movement not detected
description: Remote service use between internal hosts did not generate alerts or response during the exercise.
impact: Attackers can spread through the network without being noticed.
remediation: Improve endpoint and network telemetry, tune detections for remote service use and rehearse the response.

title: Excessive privileges on user and service accounts
description: Accounts held more rights than their role needs, allowing privilege escalation.
impact: Compromise of one account can lead to wide control.
remediation: Apply least privilege, review group membership regularly and protect privileged accounts with tiering.

title: Data exfiltration channel not monitored
description: Test data left the network through a web service without being flagged.
impact: Sensitive data could be removed without detection.
remediation: Add egress filtering and data-loss monitoring for unsanctioned web services.
